label: Surfaces
notes: Open the surfaces chapter. A complex surface is a two-complex-dimensional algebraic variety. The deck follows printed pages 469 through 646. This chapter develops intersection numbers on surfaces, the Hodge index theorem, the Picard-Lefschetz formula for monodromy, the Enriques-Kodaira classification by Kodaira dimension, and the special role of rational and ruled surfaces.

label: Intersection Form
notes: Discuss the intersection form on a surface. The symmetric bilinear pairing on the Picard group records how divisors meet. For a smooth projective surface, the form is well-defined modulo numerical equivalence and reduces to the cup product in two-dimensional cohomology. Self-intersections and intersection numbers of curves drive the rest of the chapter.

label: Hodge Index
notes: State the Hodge index theorem. The intersection form on the Neron-Severi group of a smooth projective surface has signature one positive plus the rest negative. Equivalently, the ample cone is one-dimensional positive direction; orthogonal directions to an ample class are negative. This is a structural fingerprint of polarized surface geometry.

label: Picard-Lefschetz
notes: Present the Picard-Lefschetz formula. For a family of surfaces with a single nodal degeneration, monodromy around the singular fiber acts on cohomology by a reflection in the vanishing cycle. This is the building block for monodromy representations of more complex degenerations and connects to mirror symmetry intuition.

label: Kodaira Dimension
notes: Introduce Kodaira dimension. The Kodaira dimension of a smooth projective variety classifies the asymptotic growth of pluricanonical sections: H zero of m K. For surfaces it takes values negative infinity, zero, one, and two. The Enriques-Kodaira classification organizes surfaces by this discrete invariant.

label: Rational and Ruled
notes: Cover rational and ruled surfaces. A ruled surface is a smooth projective surface with a morphism to a curve whose fibers are projective lines. A rational surface is birational to projective two-space. These form the Kodaira-dimension-minus-infinity bucket and include Hirzebruch surfaces as the basic family.

label: Recap
notes: Close with the surface toolkit. Intersection form gives the bilinear data; Hodge index pins down signature; Picard-Lefschetz tracks monodromy; Kodaira dimension classifies asymptotically; rational and ruled surfaces are the most elementary class. The next chapter on residues uses these tools for global complex-analytic statements.
